last_transition_reason: The proof correctly verifies the integrality of the exponents, rewrites the denominator (q^(2d);q^(2d))_k via 1-q^(2dj)=(1-q^(dj))(1+q^(dj)), performs the cancellation against U_{d,n}(q), obtains the stated expanded formula for G_{d,r,n}(q), and then checks each resulting term lies in Z[q,q^(-1)]. This matches the lemma sketch and the assembly role.
latest_nl_proof: Write E_k := k(d-dk-2r)/2 and F := r(1-n)/2. First, E_k is an integer because E_k = d k(1-k)/2 - kr and k(1-k) is always even. Also F is an integer because n ≡ 1 (mod 2d) implies n = 1 + 2dt for some integer t, hence F = -rdt. For any positive integer M, [M]_q = (1-q^M)/(1-q) = 1 + q + ... + q^(M-1), so [3dk+r]_q and [rn]_q lie in Z[q] (here 3dk+r > 0 and rn > 0). Moreover, for each k >= 0, (q^r,q^r,q^d; q^(2d))_k = product_{j=0}^{k-1} (1-q^(r+2dj))^2 (1-q^(d+2dj)) belongs to Z[q], and (q^d; q^d)_k = product_{j=1}^k (1-q^(dj)) belongs to Z[q]. Also U_{d,n}(q) = product_{j=1}^{n-1} (1+q^(dj)) belongs to Z[q]. Now expand G_{d,r,n}(q) = U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q)) = U_{d,n}(q)T_{d,r,n}(q) - U_{d,n}(q)R_{d,r,n}(q) in Q(q). For the k-th summand of U_{d,n}(q)T_{d,r,n}(q), use (q^(2d); q^(2d))_k = product_{j=1}^k (1-q^(2dj)) = product_{j=1}^k (1-q^(dj))(1+q^(dj)). Then U_{d,n}(q) * (q^d; q^d)_k^2 / (q^(2d); q^(2d))_k = [product_{j=1}^{n-1} (1+q^(dj))] [product_{j=1}^k (1-q^(dj))^2] / [product_{j=1}^k (1-q^(dj))(1+q^(dj))] = [product_{j=1}^k (1-q^(dj))] [product_{j=k+1}^{n-1} (1+q^(dj))] = (q^d; q^d)_k product_{j=k+1}^{n-1} (1+q^(dj)), where the product is 1 if k = n-1. Therefore G_{d,r,n}(q) = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d; q^(2d))_k (q^d; q^d)_k q^(E_k) product_{j=k+1}^{n-1} (1+q^(dj)) - U_{d,n}(q)[rn]_q q^F, which is exactly the expanded expression stated in the lemma. Finally, each summand in that finite sum lies in Z[q,q^(-1)]: all factors other than q^(E_k) lie in Z[q], while q^(E_k) is a Laurent monomial because E_k is an integer. Likewise U_{d,n}(q)[rn]_q q^F lies in Z[q,q^(-1)]. Since Z[q,q^(-1)] is closed under finite sums and differences, G_{d,r,n}(q) belongs to Z[q,q^(-1)]. Hence the lemma is proved.
role_in_parent: Builds the cleared Laurent-polynomial difference to which the theorem-specific divisibility bottleneck applies.
statement_nl: Let [m]_q=(1-q^m)/(1-q). For any parameter u and integer k>=0, let (u;q)_k:=∏_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-u q^j), and let (u,v,w;q)_k:=(u;q)_k(v;q)_k(w;q)_k. Suppose d and r are positive integers with gcd(d,r)=1 and r <= d, and suppose n>1 satisfies n ≡ 1 mod 2d. Define U_{d,n}(q):=∏_{j=1}^{n-1}(1+q^{dj}), define T_{d,r,n}(q):=∑_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}/(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k, define R_{d,r,n}(q):=[rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2}, and define G_{d,r,n}(q):=U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q)) in Q(q), where k(d-dk-2r)/2 and r(1-n)/2 are integers. Then G_{d,r,n}(q) belongs to Z[q,q^{-1}]. Equivalently, in Q(q) one has G_{d,r,n}(q)=∑_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} ∏_{j=k+1}^{n-1}(1+q^{dj}) - U_{d,n}(q) R_{d,r,n}(q), and the right-hand side is a Laurent polynomial in q.

domain_restrictions: d and r must be positive integers.
The greatest common divisor of d and r must be 1.
r must be at most d.
n must be an integer greater than 1.
n must satisfy n congruent to 1 modulo 2d.
The exponent k(d-dk-2r)/2 is intended to be an integer for each summand.
The exponent r(1-n)/2 is intended to be an integer.
q is treated as a formal indeterminate, with expressions interpreted in the rational function field in q.
Finite products over empty index sets are implicitly equal to 1.
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every positive integers d and r that are coprime, with r at most d, and every integer n greater than 1 that is congruent to 1 modulo 2d, the rational function G built from the stated finite products and sum is actually a Laurent polynomial in q with integer coefficients. The expanded equivalent expression is the same claim written in a different algebraic form.
quantifier_order: For every integer m, the q-bracket of m is defined by the given formula.
For every parameter u and every nonnegative integer k, the q-Pochhammer symbols are defined by the given finite products.
For every positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r) equal to 1 and r at most d, and every integer n greater than 1 with n congruent to 1 modulo 2d, the expressions U, T, R, and G are defined.
For those d, r, and n, the claim is that G is a Laurent polynomial with integer coefficients.
